reason: This is a FOPO brand-launch page. Taking the question at its word ('works with one cable'), no FOPO screen we link belongs in the top three. 1) S11: our without-drivers page records FOPO saying 'one USB-C cable for both is not supported'; each screen needs its own video link. 2) S7 and S1: each of the two screens needs its own video connection (our pages, citing FOPO). 3) S788 triple: it needs FOPO's UsbDisplay driver and ships with an external PD power supply, and no source shows one cable running all three screens. 4) S10: still unread. fopomonitor.com returned HTTP 429 to storecheck and WebFetch again on 2026-11-21, and a direct read of the store's product JSON was not approved. The top three that the sources support are: Mobile Pixels Duex Max DS (one added screen on one USB-C DP Alt Mode cable, no driver, our link); KYY X90E (two screens on one cable with no driver, Windows only, 2.2 kg, per TechRadar, no link); and Xebec Tri-Screen 3 (one cable on Windows ports with DisplayPort or Thunderbolt 3+; Macs need Xebec's $59 DisplayLink Mac Adapter, per Xebec's port table and store, 2026-11-21). Trio 3 Pro gets one cable only with Mobile Pixels' driver, plus a power adapter for full brightness (Macworld). Before reopening this page, re-read FOPO's S10 and S788C pages once the store stops rate-limiting. A FOPO dual that runs both screens from one USB-C cable (MST on Windows) would change this.
why_angle: Angle C is the strongest sourced finding. None of the pages ChatGPT got states that every two-screen, one-cable setup on a Mac needs an adapter or driver: Xebec's port table requires the Mac Adapter on every Mac port, and TechRadar finds the KYY X90E Windows-only. So a driver-free single cable on a MacBook means one added screen. It isn't used because the page fails the FOPO brand-launch condition.
